The current opening, body, and ending all label neutral carriers as method schematics rather than capability or result proof, while retaining the no-use fallbacks for unresolved original footage.

gates.name: Coverage
evidence: directing-brief.json covers account role and stage, audience, bounded demand clue, one search/save job and one trust guardrail, click/delivery/follow/action contracts, narrative mechanism, claim ledger, carrier and referent plans, timed beats and shots, packaging, production, experiment, assets, unknowns, safety, and rights.
brief.md supplies the post-publication review order and separates execution compliance from whether the direction is supported.

Price, compatibility, analytics availability, actual device/tool, original UI-display rights, and final-clip nested rights remain explicit unknowns with owners and resolution or mandatory no-use paths.

gates.name: Evidence fidelity
evidence: claim_demand remains a user_claim used only as a topic clue and expressly cannot support population demand, search volume, priority, or conversion.

claim_dependency now attributes only the Codex + Flova dependency to the task and separately labels human fact/rights checking as this production's responsibility; linked opening speech, shots, and Markdown preserve that distinction.

Price and compatibility remain unknown; the import and cover schematics are explicitly not capability proof; the task-stated final clip is not promoted to quality, automation, performance, or causal evidence.
No public metric, single operation, schematic, or source assertion is upgraded to a causal conclusion.

gates.name: Promise closure
evidence: Title, cover, first frame, and opening agree on a pre-use four-item verification checklist and disclose Flova within the first four seconds and again within the first 12 seconds.
The delivery contract and body now promise only verification actions and evidence boundaries: check current price/system evidence, run one's own file test, and make/check a candidate cover manually.
The ending closes those same four actions and states that the neutral clip is a method schematic rather than a project result; it no longer reports a demonstrated single-file result.
The save CTA is tied to the delivered checklist, and the follow contract names bounded future value: later rights/evidence-closed tests, failures, and human corrections.

gates.name: Executability
evidence: Six beats and linked shots specify durations totaling 76 seconds, exact speech, on-screen text, visual content, cognitive/function roles, evidence responsibility, asset references, transitions, and edit decisions.

The creator owns fact checking, asset creation, narration, editing, rights review, publishing, and measurement; the production section supplies tools, locations, a 255-minute allocation, and explicit failure/no-evidence fallbacks.
Packaging, one CTA, anonymous comment coding, metric definitions and proxies, observation windows, confounds, and review sequence make capture, edit, publish, and measurement actions identifiable.

gates.name: Production feasibility
evidence: The public cut depends only on creator-owned neutral diagrams/animations, the creator's own markdown file, and self-recorded voice; unresolved original UI footage and the original final clip are not production dependencies.

One creator, ordinary screen/voice/edit tools, two desk environments, a 70-82-second target, and 255 scheduled minutes are plausible within the stated half day if the schematic animation remains simple.
Unavailable current facts, a failed internal file test, and unresolved rights each trigger a bounded content change or mandatory safe substitute.

gates.name: Original transfer
evidence: The task supplies no reference creator or source work, so the originality transfer exception is correctly recorded as not applicable instead of inventing inspiration.

The executable plan uses creator-owned wording, diagrams, files, footage, and voice and prohibits copied identity elements, proprietary wording, unverifiable case ownership, and identifiable comments.

gates.name: Measurement
evidence: singlePlan.experiment declares exactly one primary variable, opening; both versions are fixed at 12 seconds and both must disclose Codex + Flova dependency and this production's human-checking responsibility within that interval.
Audience, body order, neutral assets and proof boundaries, title/cover hierarchy, CTA, total duration, and publishing conditions are locked.

Save rate matches the search/save job; 12-second retention and tool-misattribution comments are guardrails; the plan includes 24-hour/7-day windows, a four-post minimum, proxy definitions, non-random confounds, and retain/undecided/change rules.

gates.name: Safety and rights
evidence: The executable public asset graph is limited to seven creator-owned assets; the original Flova UI/logo recording remains prohibited until applicable terms or written permission are confirmed and archived.

The original final clip remains prohibited until every nested visual, track, font, likeness, UI/logo, and generated element is inventoried and cleared; an unauthorized item requires removal/replacement and re-audit, with a creator-owned neutral clip as fallback.

The plan excludes comment identities, private messages, and unavailable conversion data; uses no music/effects/ambient track; scopes time-sensitive price and compatibility claims; prohibits free, universal, automatic, traffic, or causal promises; and assigns pre-publication commercial disclosure review.

judgeScores.evidence: The pre-use checklist fits the early account's practical AI-use promise, a clearly bounded independent-creator audience, and the search/save job; the demand basis remains only a supplied four-question clue, so distinctiveness is useful rather than validated.
judgeScores.revision: After publication, use anonymous question coding and save behavior to decide which one of the four checks deserves a deeper evidence-led episode.

judgeScores.evidence: The sequence moves from dependency correction to a four-item map, current-fact verification, file-test method, cover transfer, and explicit closure; every shot states its proof responsibility and the neutral carriers do not impersonate real results.
judgeScores.revision: If later rights-cleared observable evidence becomes available, replace one schematic with one tightly scoped real state transition while retaining the current cannot-support language.

judgeScores.evidence: Every carrier and transition has a defined cognitive function, durations sum cleanly to 76 seconds, and the no-music design is feasible; the opening's three-way split plus two evidence-category labels creates the main visual-load risk.
judgeScores.revision: Prototype the first four seconds at phone size and simplify the split or label count if either dependency or responsibility cannot be read once without pausing.

judgeScores.evidence: The searchable title names both tools and the decision moment, the cover exposes four concrete subquestions, the save CTA matches the job, and the comment taxonomy supports series routing without treating comments as representative demand.
judgeScores.revision: Before publishing, verify that the final title and on-screen terms match the current product naming and the creator's actual device wording; do not add unsupported price or compatibility keywords.

judgeScores.evidence: A pre-investment creator can understand the boundary quickly, leave with four actions, and avoid false claims about free access, compatibility, automatic editing, or demonstrated success; the content intentionally trades spectacle for trust and reusable checking.
judgeScores.revision: Use the end card as a genuinely readable checklist and allow enough silent hold time for a viewer to capture all four actions.

judgeScores.evidence: The plan names one variable, matching main/guardrail metrics, proxies, windows, minimum evidence, confounds, and explicit retain/stop/undecided rules; it correctly acknowledges that four non-random posts cannot establish causality.
